questions.text: Under the Indian Constitution, the power to legislate on 'Inter-State Trade and Commerce' resides with:

options.label: C
options.text: Both Parliament and State Legislature (Concurrent List)

options.label: D
options.text: Neither; it is a residuary subject

questions.solution: Shortcut: Article 301-307 (Part XIII) deal with Trade/Commerce. 'Inter-State' implies movement across borders, a classic Union subject (Entry 42, Union List) to ensure economic unity. 'Intra-State' trade is State subject (Entry 26, State List). Option C (Concurrent) applies to subjects like Education, Forests. Detailed: Article 246 read with Seventh Schedule. Union List Entry 42: 'Inter-State trade and commerce'. Parliament has exclusive power (Article 246(1)). State List Entry 26 covers 'Trade and commerce within the State'. The Constitution (Articles 301-304) guarantees freedom of inter-state trade subject to Parliament's regulatory power.

questions.text: With reference to the Indian Freedom Struggle, which one of the following statements about the 'August Offer' (1940) is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It proposed the immediate transfer of power to an interim Indian government.

options.label: B
options.text: It recognized the right of Indians to frame their own Constitution after the war.

options.label: C
options.text: It accepted the demand for a separate Constituent Assembly for the Muslim League.

options.label: D
options.text: It offered Dominion Status to India immediately upon the declaration of war.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options promising 'immediate' transfer or Dominion Status (A, D) as the British delayed both. Option C (separate Assembly) was the Cripps Mission (1942) / Cabinet Mission (1946) era demand. The August Offer (Viceroy Linlithgow) explicitly recognized for the first time the inherent right of Indians to frame their own Constitution post-war. Detailed: The August Offer 1940 aimed to secure Indian cooperation in WWII. Key points: 1. Dominion Status as objective (not immediate). 2. Expansion of Viceroy's Executive Council. 3. **Crucially: Recognition of the right of Indians to frame their own Constitution after the war.** 4. Assurance to minorities (veto power). It was rejected by Congress and Muslim League.

questions.text: Select the word that correctly completes the sentence: 'The _____ of the glass broke easily when dropped.'
questions.solution: 'Brittleness' is the property of being liable to break or shatter, fitting the context of glass. 'Ductility' and 'malleability' apply to metals that can be drawn into wires or hammered. 'Viscosity' refers to fluid thickness.

questions.text: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error: "Neither the manager nor the employees was aware of the new policy."
questions.solution: Shortcut: In a "neither…nor" construction the verb agrees with the noun nearest to it ("employees" – plural), so the verb must be plural ("were"). The singular "was" is therefore the error. Full solution: The subject closer to the verb is "employees" (plural). The correct verb form is "were aware". Hence the segment "was aware" (option C) carries the grammatical mistake.

questions.text: Find out which part of the sentence has an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. Each of the students who have passed the examination (A) / are eligible to apply (B) / for the scholarship scheme. (C) / No Error (D)

options.label: A
options.text: Each of the students who have passed the examination

questions.solution: Shortcut: Identify the main subject ('Each of the students') which is always singular. Ignore the relative clause ('who have passed...') where 'who' refers to plural 'students'. The main verb must agree with the singular subject 'Each', so 'are' is incorrect; it should be 'is'. Step-by-step: The subject 'Each of the students' is a singular distributive pronoun phrase requiring a singular verb. The clause 'who have passed' correctly uses plural 'have' because 'who' refers to 'students'. However, the main verb in part (B) 'are eligible' is plural, disagreeing with the singular subject 'Each'. The correct verb is 'is eligible'. Hence, the error lies in part (B).

questions.text: The table shows the Decadal Population Growth Rate (%) for India across three decades. By what percentage points did the growth rate decline from 1991-2001 to 2001-2011? | Decade | Growth Rate (%) | |---|---| | 1981-1991 | 23.9 | | 1991-2001 | 21.5 | | 2001-2011 | 17.7 |
questions.solution: Shortcut: Direct subtraction of decimals. 21.5 - 17.7. Subtract whole numbers: 21-17=4. Subtract decimals: 0.5-0.7 = -0.2. Result = 4 - 0.2 = 3.8. Option elimination: 2.4 is 21.5-19.1. 4.2 is 21.9-17.7. 5.6 is 23.3-17.7. Worked: Decline = Growth Rate (1991-2001) - Growth Rate (2001-2011) = 21.5% - 17.7% = 3.8 percentage points.

questions.text: At which session of the Indian National Congress was the resolution for 'Poorna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) adopted, and who presided over that session?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Link 'Poorna Swaraj' to the iconic 1929 Lahore session where Nehru hoisted the tricolor on the banks of Ravi; Karachi 1931 endorsed Gandhi-Irwin Pact, Lucknow 1916 was Congress-League Pact, Tripuri 1939 saw Bose's resignation. Full Solution: The Lahore Session (Dec 1929) under President Jawaharlal Nehru passed the Poorna Swaraj resolution, declaring Jan 26, 1930 as Independence Day. Karachi 1931 (Patel) ratified the Gandhi-Irwin Pact. Tripuri 1939 (Bose) witnessed the crisis over Bose's presidency.

questions.text: Identify the synonym of the word 'Candid'.
questions.solution: 'Candid' means truthful and straightforward. 'Honest' is a direct synonym. 'Deceitful' and 'Secretive' are antonyms, while 'Angry' is unrelated to the definition.

questions.text: The Battle of Plassey, a decisive victory for the British East India Company over the Nawab of Bengal, was fought in which year?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Chronological anchoring. 1757 (Plassey) -> 1764 (Buxar) -> 1857 (Revolt). 1761 is Third Battle of Panipat (Marathas vs Abdali). Plassey (1757) established Company rule in Bengal; Buxar (1764) confirmed it. Worked Solution: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 between the forces of the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah, and the British East India Company led by Robert Clive. The Battle of Buxar followed in 1764. The Third Battle of Panipat occurred in 1761. The Revolt of 1857 occurred a century later.

questions.text: Based on the chart showing the share of renewable energy in total electricity generation (2021), which region contributes the smallest percentage?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Identify the shortest bar; the smallest visual length corresponds to the lowest percentage. Full solution: The chart indicates Southeast Asia 15%, Middle East 12%, North America 8%, Europe 30%. The smallest share is North America at 8%.

questions.text: The phenomenon of 'Ocean Acidification' is primarily caused by the absorption of which gas by seawater?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Link 'Acidification' to 'Carbonic Acid'. CO2 + H2O -> H2CO3 (Carbonic Acid). This lowers pH. Methane/N2O are potent GHGs but don't dissolve to form strong acids in ocean volumes. SO2 causes acid rain (atmospheric), not primary driver of ocean acidification. Detailed: Oceans absorb ~30% of anthropogenic CO2 emissions. Dissolved CO2 reacts with water (H2O) to form carbonic acid (H2CO3), which dissociates into bicarbonate (HCO3-) and hydrogen ions (H+). Increased H+ concentration lowers pH (acidification) and reduces carbonate ion (CO3 2-) availability, harming calcifying organisms (corals, shellfish).

questions.text: Who among the following was the founder of the 'Servants of India Society' (1905), dedicated to training national missionaries for the service of India?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Associate 'Servants of India Society' with 'Gokhale' (Mentor to Gandhi, Moderate leader). Ranade was his guru (Poona Sarvajanik Sabha). Tilak was Extremist (Home Rule League). Naoroji was 'Grand Old Man' (British Indian Association, Congress President). Detailed: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in Pune (1905) with the objective of training selfless workers for national service. It focused on education, sanitation, and upliftment of depressed classes. Gokhale was a prominent moderate leader and political mentor to Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.text: From the table of world heritage sites added in 2020, which country added the most sites?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Compare the numbers column-wise; the highest digit count wins. Full solution: Italy 5 sites, China 3 sites, Mexico 2 sites, Turkey 4 sites. Italy added the most with 5 sites.

questions.text: Read the sentence to find out whether there is any grammatical error in it. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. The letter of that part is the answer. If there is no error, the answer is (D). (Ignore errors of punctuation, if any.) Neither the manager nor his subordinates (A) / has submitted the report (B) / within the stipulated deadline. (C) / No error (D)

options.label: A
options.text: Neither the manager nor his subordinates

questions.solution: Shortcut (Proximity Rule): In 'Neither...nor' constructions, the verb agrees with the subject nearest to it. Here, 'subordinates' (Plural) is closest to the verb, so the verb must be plural ('have'), not singular ('has'). Eliminate A (structure is correct), C (prepositional phrase is correct), and D (error exists). Full Solution: The sentence uses the correlative conjunction 'Neither...nor'. According to the Rule of Proximity (or Concord), when two subjects are joined by 'neither...nor', 'either...or', 'not only...but also', the verb agrees in number and person with the subject nearest to it. In part (B), the verb 'has submitted' is singular. However, the nearest subject is 'his subordinates', which is plural. Therefore, the correct verb should be 'have submitted'. The error lies in part (B).

questions.text: Which of the following phenomena explains the formation of the 'Thar Desert' in Rajasthan?

options.label: A
options.text: Rain shadow effect of the Western Ghats

options.label: B
options.text: Cold ocean current along the western coast

options.label: C
options.text: Divergence of the Arabian Sea branch of the Monsoon and the Aravalli range running parallel to it

options.label: D
options.text: High pressure belt permanently situated over North-West India

questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate geographical mismatches. Western Ghats (Option A) affect the Deccan plateau, not Rajasthan. Cold currents (Option B) affect coastal deserts (Atacama/Namib), not inland Thar. Permanent High Pressure (Option D) is a general subtropical feature, not the specific dynamic cause for Thar's aridity. The specific mechanism is the Aravalli range running SW-NE, parallel to the SW Monsoon winds (Arabian Sea branch), preventing orographic lift and causing rain shadow/divergence. Full Solution: The Aravalli Hills run parallel to the direction of the Arabian Sea branch of the South-West Monsoon (South-West to North-East). They do not act as a barrier to intercept the moisture-laden winds. Consequently, the winds pass over Rajasthan without significant orographic rainfall, creating the Thar Desert. This is a classic case of 'Parallel Range Effect' rather than a standard Rain Shadow (which requires perpendicular ranges).
